source.review_note: Composition of seven exact approved hash-bound procedures. Frame access/closure retained once; approved bench renewal sections inserted at the exposed-frame cutpoint. Throttle grip cable-end access separates throttle body from bar group while hydraulics stay closed. Independent composition-order review pending. Root independently reviewed all150 mechanical cutpoints and approved the exact combined scope after corrected verification text, source-footer labels, explicit new bearing stacks and early grip-end detach with supported bar. No physical validation claimed.

title: Strip to the frame, renew chassis bearings and reassemble the bike
completeness: Assembled exact stock bike to serviceable exposed main frame with steering races removed, then renewal of steering, both wheel, swingarm/linkage and sealed shock-eye bearings and bike reassembly. Throttle grip cable ends detached/refitted; closed hydraulic assemblies remain supported together. Engine internals, fork/shock internals, structural repair and bonded frame pads are separate.

applicability.included: Exact stockUS2026YZ450F; serviceable original frame, engine, wheel hubs, swingarm/linkage and sealed suspension assemblies; new exact bearing/seal parts listed. No automatic other-year inheritance.
excluded: Structural frame repair, welding, straightening, alignment correction or bonded-pad removal
Hydraulic joint opening or master/caliper overhaul
Complete throttle cable replacement or throttle-body end detachment
Modified harness/routing preventing supported closed hydraulic assembly removal

prerequisites: Match the exact bike and installed stock parts. Have the complete cited diagrams available.
Stable maintenance stand and support suitable for changing weight distribution; clean labeled parts storage.
Both correct stock replacement bearing/race sets and dust seal available; verify against actual assemblies before destructive removal.

Motion Pro08-0544 driver must clear cage and load only fitted inner ring;08-0669 must fit each head race and pass through this frame. Inspect actual fit; model-specific tool compatibility is not asserted.
Confirm replacement parts match actual stock assemblies before removal. Verify bearing tool mandrels, receiver and puller fit each joint; no08-0294 model fit is asserted.
Engine separately supported while pivot removed; shock upper mount is removed later and restored once after eye renewal.
Verify new OEM-equivalent stock eye components and actual mandrel/receiver fit before removal. Do not transfer tool fit from another model.
Support the mounting eye locally; never transmit pressing load through the shock rod or pressure body.
Inspect the removed wheel before bearing work; unrelated wheel/tire/disc defects require separate repair.
Front-wheel puller/driver must clear its retained disc; front disc bolts remain untouched. Rear disc is separately removed/refitted in this route.
No known cable damage or pre-existing abnormal idle.
Keep cable outer routing and body-end adjustment unchanged.
If composed into another job, complete that job and restore all assemblies before the running-check range.
All bearing renewal parts and actual fitting tool/adapter checks must be complete before first disassembly. This single route renews the listed bearings; it does not merely inspect them.
Use independent supports for engine, frame, wheels, bar and every closed hydraulic assembly. No hose, cable or engine rear mount carries unsupported component weight.
Engine stays internally assembled; any independently performed internal job requires its own documented pre-start checks before refit.

critical_stop_conditions: Unstable support, bent/cracked parts, damaged fasteners or unknown assembly order.
Binding, leaks, missing hardware or abnormal brake/control function remains an unresolved fault.

steps.title: Record the engine and job condition
steps.instruction: Record the exact stock engine identity, running condition and reason for removal. Photograph hose, electrical and bracket routing before access. Prepare an independently supported engine bench and a controlled lift with a helper; this guide removes/installs the assembly and does not repair its internals.
verification: Engine identity, fault and lift/support plan recorded.

steps.title: Record the original cable positions
steps.instruction: Record the pull and return cable positions at the grip against the page 4-39 diagram. Record existing grip free play, which must be 3–6 mm before this service. Preserve the outer cable routing and adjustment so neither cable is swapped on refit.
verification: Pull/return identities, routing and initial free play recorded.

steps.title: Drain the engine oil before lifting
steps.instruction: For a normally running engine, follow the oil-change warm-up then stop the engine; do not run a faulted engine solely to warm oil. Stand the bike upright, place drain containers and remove the filler cap and both oil drain bolts. Drain tank and crankcase. Leave the oil filter unchanged unless separately serviced. Install new drain-bolt gaskets: tank bolt 10 N·m, crankcase bolt 20 N·m. Mark the engine empty of oil.
verification: Oil drained; two new gaskets; tank 10/crankcase 20 N·m; engine marked empty.

steps.title: Prepare the bike
steps.instruction: Stop the engine, let it cool and support the bike. Clean the intake and fuel work area. Keep dirt out of open joints and fuel work away from ignition sources.
verification: Cold engine; stable bike; clean work area; parts/tools ready.

steps.title: Open the sub-seat
steps.instruction: Release its quick fastener and lift the sub-seat first; it is tethered to the main seat. Open the fuel cap and transfer the tank fuel with a fuel-safe pump into a suitable container, then secure the cap.
verification: Sub-seat tether not strained; fuel contained.

steps.title: Remove access panels
steps.instruction: Remove the main-seat bolts and slide the seat rearward. Remove the left/right side covers, keeping their bolts and collars labeled. Slide the right cover out of its upper and lower locating slots instead of pulling the tabs apart.
verification: Seat and two side covers removed; hardware locations retained.

steps.title: Isolate the battery
steps.instruction: With the engine stopped, disconnect the negative battery lead first, then the positive lead. Insulate the loose terminals. Retain the battery and relay in place unless separate frame work requires removal; no starter action is allowed during the work.
verification: Negative then positive disconnected and insulated.

steps.title: Expose the tank
steps.instruction: Release the air-filter-case cover ribs by pressing the duct sides inward and lifting the rear; slide the cover rearward to release the front projection. Leave the filter installed. Remove the left/right shroud bolts and shrouds, retaining their collars.
verification: Air-filter-case cover and shrouds removed; filter undisturbed.

steps.title: Disconnect the tank
steps.instruction: Unplug the fuel-pump connector. Put cloths below and around the fuel-hose joint for residual pressure. Slide the connector cover back, press its two release buttons, and separate the joint by hand. Fit the supplied joint covers immediately to both openings.
verification: Pump disconnected; both fuel openings capped; no forced hose tools.

steps.title: Lift the tank clear
steps.instruction: Remove the tank mounting fasteners, retaining the collars/dampers in their original locations, and lift the tank away. Support it so its weight does not rest on the fuel-pump mounting surface. Leave the pump installed in the tank.
verification: Tank supported; mounts accounted for; pump untouched.

steps.title: Release the intact case
steps.instruction: Disconnect the intake-air-temperature-sensor coupler by its connector latch. Loosen the air-filter-case joint clamp screw and remove the three case mounting bolts, retaining their collars, washers and dampers at the original locations. Keep the filter, temperature sensor and case assembly bracket attached to the case.
verification: Sensor coupler disconnected; three mounting sets retained; case internals attached.

steps.title: Lift off and protect the intake
steps.instruction: Lift the case clear of its seated intake connection without loading the remaining throttle body. Protect the exposed throttle-body inlet from dirt. Keep the case clean and inspect the joint and mounting supports for visible damage. Do not push the throttle valve, loosen sensor screws or move the cables.
verification: Intact case removed; clean inlet protected; throttle and sensors undisturbed.

steps.title: Open the cable housing
steps.instruction: Pull back the rubber cover. Remove the housing screws and separate the throttle cable housing without pulling on the cables.
verification: Housing open; rubber cover and screws retained.

steps.title: Release the two grip-end cables
steps.instruction: Disengage the pull and return cable ends from their original seats in the throttle tube as shown. Support the cables without kinking them and withdraw the complete grip/tube assembly from the bar. Do not peel the bonded rubber grip off its tube or disturb the cable ends at the throttle body.
verification: Both identified ends released; intact grip/tube retained.

steps.title: Check the released parts
steps.instruction: Inspect the tube sliding surface and cable-end seats for damage and check that the cables move without binding. Keep dirt out of the open housing. A damaged or frayed cable needs a separate full cable-renewal operation before this access job can return to service.
verification: Retained parts accepted; no damaged cable or binding.

steps.title: Remove the complete silencer
steps.instruction: Support the silencer. Loosen its joint clamp, remove its two mounting bolts and lift the complete silencer off its joint. Keep the silencer body, end cap and packing assembled.
verification: Complete silencer supported and removed; internals untouched.

steps.title: Remove the intermediate pipe
steps.instruction: Loosen the pipe-2 joint clamp and remove the exhaust-pipe bracket bolt while supporting the pipe. Move pipe 2 through the clearance path shown in PDF211 and remove it without forcing nearby components.
verification: Pipe 2 removed; mounting hardware retained.

steps.title: Remove the header and old seals
steps.instruction: Remove the header nuts and header pipe. Leave the header protector attached. Remove the old head gasket and the two pipe-joint gaskets; inspect joint faces and supports for damage before refitting.
verification: Header removed; all three separated joint seals identified; protector untouched.

steps.title: Set up for a cold drain
steps.instruction: Stand the cooled bike upright on a level surface. Place the collection container beneath the engine and position it close to the drain outlet, because flow can shoot sideways when the radiator cap is released.
verification: Bike stable; engine and coolant cold; collection ready.

steps.title: Open the drain and radiator cap
steps.instruction: Remove the coolant drain bolt and its copper washer. Place a thick cloth over the radiator cap and turn it slowly counterclockwise toward its detent to release residual pressure. Once hissing stops, press down and turn farther to remove the cap. Let the coolant drain into the container.
verification: Drain complete; old washer removed; cap opened only when cold.

steps.title: Install a new drain washer
steps.instruction: Install a new copper washer and the coolant drain bolt. Tighten the bolt to 10 N·m.
verification: New washer installed; drain bolt 10 N·m.

steps.title: Disconnect the engine coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Identify radiator hoses 1,3 and 4 from the source drawing. Mark each hose and clamp position, loosen its engine-side clamp and release the hoses from the engine. Keep radiators mounted and protect the open hose/engine ports from dirt. Do not remove coolant pipe joints or the temperature sensor itself.
verification: Hoses 1/3/4 labeled and clear; pipe joints/sensor remain sealed.

steps.title: Lift the intact throttle body from the engine joint
steps.instruction: Clean the lower intake joint, loosen its clamp and lift the intact throttle body clear. The grip-end cables were detached earlier; support the body and both identified cables separately outside the engine lifting path without tension. Keep body-end cable seats, sensors, adjustment screws and pulley intact; protect the engine intake and housing against dirt.
verification: Throttle body supported clear; cables/sensors undisturbed; intake protected.

steps.title: Disconnect the left engine harness interfaces
steps.instruction: Release only the retaining clips/ties needed to free engine leads. Disconnect the stator, crankshaft-position and gear-position connectors; keep the gear-position switch bolted to the engine so its seal is not disturbed. Match connector identity to the diagrams, including the white 3-pin gear-position and gray 2-pin stator connectors. Label and protect both halves.
verification: Stator/crank-position/gear-position leads released; sensor seals untouched.

steps.title: Disconnect starter, ground and plug interfaces
steps.instruction: Disconnect the coolant-temperature connector, pull the spark-plug cap clear without removing the plug, and remove the engine-ground terminal bolt. At the starter lead, hold the motor-side terminal nut with a spanner while undoing the lead nut. Release the lead clamps and support the harness away from the lift path.
verification: Ground/starter/temperature/plug disconnected; starter terminal not twisted.

steps.title: Remove chain, sprocket and shift pedal
steps.instruction: Remove the sprocket cover. Release the stock clip-type chain joint and remove the chain; retain the matched link/plate and prepare a new clip. Remove the sprocket nut and old lock washer using an appropriate holding tool, then remove the sprocket. Mark and remove the shift pedal; retain its bolt and original punch-mark alignment.
verification: Chain and sprocket clear; old lock washer/clip retired; shift position recorded.

steps.title: Unbolt the intact clutch release unit
steps.instruction: Protect the clutch lever from operation. Support the release body and remove its two mount bolts while keeping its hydraulic hose attached. Retain the washer, remove the old mounting O-ring and leave push rod 2 and its shaft oil seal installed. Support the unit outside the lifting path without stressing the hose.
verification: Closed release unit supported; washer retained; new mounting O-ring ready.

steps.title: Clear pedal, guard and breather
steps.instruction: Remove the engine guard, brake-pedal pivot bolt and return spring. Support the pedal with its master-cylinder linkage attached. Label and release the cylinder-head breather hose from the engine and its routing holders. Keep brake hydraulics closed.
verification: Guard/pedal/spring retained; breather clear; brake system closed.

steps.title: Support engine and swingarm before undoing mounts
steps.instruction: Support the engine independently. Support the swingarm and prepare a same-diameter temporary support shaft from its other side if needed when the pivot is withdrawn. Confirm every electrical connector, hose, intake assembly and cable is clear before loosening the engine mounts.
verification: Independent supports ready; all engine interfaces clear.

steps.title: Release the engine mounts
steps.instruction: Remove the left/right upper brackets and two lower brackets with their identified hardware, keeping bolt positions separate. Withdraw the pivot while maintaining swingarm support. Keep the engine fully supported as the last mounting fasteners come out; never let it hang from a remaining hose or lead.
verification: Mount hardware mapped; pivot removed with swingarm supported.

steps.title: Lift the engine out to the right
steps.instruction: Lift the engine and move its lower part toward the right side of the chassis as shown in the OEM drawing, then transfer it to the prepared support. Stop if any interface catches. Keep the inlet, exhaust and fluid ports protected from contamination.
verification: Assembly removed to right; no trapped interface; engine stable.

steps.title: Support the rear wheel
steps.instruction: Keep the chassis independently supported with its rear wheel clear. The engine and drive chain are already removed. Protect the rear brake pedal against operation while the wheel is absent; keep the hydraulic line closed.
verification: Rear wheel clear, bike stable, brake pedal protected.

steps.title: Release the axle and chain
steps.instruction: Remove the rear axle nut. Loosen both adjuster locknuts and turn the adjusting bolts inward. Support the wheel, withdraw the axle and retain both pullers and collars by side. The chain was already removed for engine access; lower the wheel clear without disturbing the hydraulic line.
verification: Wheel clear; left/right pullers and collars labeled.

steps.title: Inspect wheel, axle and collars
steps.instruction: Check the axle for bending, the tire/wheel and collars for damage, and bearings for roughness or looseness. Inspect seals and sprocket teeth. Record defects; damaged components need the matching repair before refitting.
verification: Serviceability recorded; no damaged parts silently reused.

steps.title: Free the complete rear brake assembly
steps.instruction: With the rear wheel removed, slide the complete caliper/bracket off its swingarm guide and release the hose retaining clamps. The pedal pivot/spring were already removed during engine access. Remove the two rear-master-cylinder mounting bolts and support master, hose, caliper and linked pedal together. Keep hose unions, reservoir, pads and pushrod pin attached; do not pump the pedal.
verification: Entire rear brake assembly supported off frame/swingarm; hydraulic circuit remains closed.

steps.title: Unlink the shock and linkage
steps.instruction: Support the swingarm independently. Remove the lower shock bolt and keep the shock supported on its unchanged upper mount. Remove the connecting-arm frame bolt, connecting-arm-to-relay bolt and relay-to-swingarm bolt, keeping each fastener and collar/washer stack associated with its joint. Keep the detached linkage joints identified for the renewal stage.
verification: Swingarm cannot drop; three linkage joints and lower shock joint identified.

steps.title: Remove the supported swingarm
steps.instruction: The engine pivot is already withdrawn. Support the arm while removing the temporary support shaft used for engine removal, then lower the swingarm clear. Keep original collars and thrust-bearing/seal stacks with their correct sides. The linkage is already free; bearing/seal renewal follows the bare-frame inspection.
verification: Temporary pivot removed; supported arm clear; all stacks labeled.

steps.title: Inspect the arm, pivot and linkage
steps.instruction: Inspect swingarm and linkage arms for cracks, bending and damaged bearing bores. Roll the pivot on a flat surface to check straightness; never straighten a bent pivot. Record condition of bushes, collars, thrust bearings and washers. Replace damaged structural parts before installing new bearings. Bearing/bushing and linkage bearing/collar pairs are renewed as sets.
verification: Serviceability recorded for pivot, arm and every linkage joint.

steps.title: Remove the sealed shock
steps.instruction: Support the shock, remove its upper nut/bolt and lift out the complete sealed assembly. Its lower bolt was removed with the linkage. Keep the eyelet stacks identified until their bench renewal; do not release gas or loosen the preload hardware.
verification: Sealed shock and upper hardware supported and retained.

steps.title: Record and support
steps.instruction: Record both fork clicker settings and current height before front-end removal; this operation restores standard2 mm projection. Keep the stripped chassis independently supported with its front wheel clear. The engine and rear wheel are already removed.
verification: Bike stable; original setup recorded; standard-height target understood.

steps.title: Free the hose guides
steps.instruction: Remove the number-plate bolt, release the brake hose from its upper/lower guides, then pull the plate projection free of the front fender. Keep the hose routed and unstressed.
verification: Plate removed; guide routing recorded.

steps.title: Support the intact handlebar assembly
steps.instruction: Mark the existing bar position. Remove the handlebar protector and the four upper-holder bolts, then lift the bar from its holders and support it without loading the cables or hydraulic hoses. The throttle grip/tube and its cable ends are already detached and identified. Keep the remaining controls and closed hydraulic hoses attached; do not loosen the lower-holder nuts. With the fork legs still clamped, loosen the steering-stem nut for later removal.
verification: Bar position recorded; complete bar supported with cables/hoses unstressed.

steps.title: Remove the front wheel
steps.instruction: Loosen all four axle pinch bolts. Support the wheel; remove the axle nut and axle, then lower the wheel clear. Label and retain its left and right collars. Prevent the brake lever being operated with the disc absent.
verification: Wheel/axle/collars retained with correct sides; pads not forced closed.

steps.title: Support the brake assembly
steps.instruction: Remove the two caliper mounting bolts and support the complete caliper so its weight cannot pull on the hose. Keep the hose union, bleed screw, pad pin and pads undisturbed. Release the brake-hose holder from the fork protector, preserving its orientation and paint-mark position.
verification: Caliper supported; closed hydraulic circuit; hose not loaded.

steps.title: Remove the protectors
steps.instruction: Remove the three protector bolts on each fork leg and lift the protectors away. Keep the hardware grouped by side.
verification: Both protectors removed; hardware accounted for.

steps.title: Release each fork leg
steps.instruction: Support one fork leg. Loosen its upper-clamp pinch bolts, then use the specified ring wrench to loosen—but not remove—the damper assembly at the top while the lower clamp still holds the leg. Loosen the lower-clamp pinch bolts and slide the supported leg down and out. Repeat on the other side; keep assemblies upright and intact.
verification: Both legs supported and removed; caps only loosened; no oil drained or internal components removed.

steps.title: Check before refitting
steps.instruction: Keep the assemblies intact. Check for visible leakage, damage or abnormal movement. A fork that needs repair does not become serviced by completing this removal/refit task; route it to the separate repair operation.
verification: Assemblies suitable for refit or fault recorded; internal-service status not invented.

steps.title: Remove the front fender
steps.instruction: Remove its four bolts and retain the mounting hardware in order. Remove the steering-stem nut and lift away the upper bracket and its washer.
verification: Fender, upper bracket and washer retained; all supported.

steps.title: Lower the steering stem
steps.instruction: Support the lower bracket. Remove the ring nut using the steering-nut wrench, then lower the stem and retain the upper bearing and race cover. Photograph the lower seal and bearing stack and both head race orientations before disturbing them.
verification: Lower bracket supported and removed; bearing stack retained in order.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the steering bearings
steps.instruction: Clean and inspect the exposed steering seats, stem and upper/lower brackets. Record damage, pitting, cracks or bending. Replace structurally damaged parts before continuing; do not repair a damaged seat by forcing a new race into it.
verification: Retained brackets/stem and seats inspected; both old bearing/race sets are scheduled for renewal, not reuse.

steps.title: Remove the old matched bearing sets
steps.instruction: Following Yamaha PDF182 illustrations, remove each head-pipe race with the long rod and hammer, and remove the lower bracket bearing race with the chisel and hammer. Keep the stem and frame protected. Discard the removed bearing/race sets. Clean the exposed seats and inspect for damage before installing replacements.
verification: Both old head races and lower bearing removed without seat/stem damage
New bearings and races retained as matched sets

steps.title: Remove the radiators and remaining hose connections
steps.instruction: Coolant was drained during engine access. Label all four hoses1–4 and every remaining clamp orientation using the source diagram. Release the remaining radiator-side hose joints and the radiator breather. Support each radiator, remove its two mounting bolts, and retain each damper/collar/washer stack. Lift both radiators and the loose hoses clear. Leave the coolant pipe joints and their O-rings on the removed engine.
verification: Both radiators/hoses labeled; four mount stacks retained; engine pipe seals untouched.

steps.title: Release the rear electrical attachments
steps.instruction: Battery leads are isolated. Release the battery band and lift out the battery. Unplug ECU, CCU and starter-relay harness couplers, releasing their covers first; retain the electronics in their original holders on the rear frame. Release the white/green-tape harness ties and clip so the main loom is free of the rear frame. Keep starter/positive leads on the relay and carry them with the rear frame; the starter lead is already free at the engine.
verification: Battery removed; rear couplers identified; loom/ties released; relay leads supported.

steps.title: Remove the rear-frame assembly
steps.instruction: Support the rear frame with rear fender/holders attached. Remove the upper chain tensioner retaining pin and washer, then slide off its roller from the rear-frame bolt; prepare a new pin. Remove all four rear-frame bolts and lift the assembly clear, checking no wire, silencer or hose remains attached. Keep each bolt with its original position.
verification: Rear-frame assembly clear; four bolts mapped; upper roller/washer retained; new pin ready.

steps.title: Lift the supported controls and main harness clear
steps.instruction: The throttle grip is off the bar and its cable ends are detached; keep the identified cables attached to the intact throttle body and independently supported. Release remaining frame/cable holders and ties using the exact routing diagrams. Unbolt rectifier/regulator, ignition-coil bracket and air-filter-case brackets, retaining connectors where possible. Lift the harness and supported bar with its closed front-brake/clutch assemblies clear; lift the separate throttle-body/cable group clear without kinking. No hose or cable bears another component's weight. Closed hydraulic lines remain attached to their supported controls; modified routing preventing this removal is outside this route.
verification: All frame holders released; intact controls/hydraulics supported; harness and brackets clear without tension.

steps.title: Remove the remaining bolt-on frame parts
steps.instruction: Remove each complete footrest bracket with its peg, spring and pin still assembled; retain the four bracket bolts by side. Remove the lower chain-tensioner bolt and intact roller/collar stack. Identify and retain any remaining clip-in harness holders and removable rubber mounting pieces in labeled positions. The steering races have been removed; bonded frame pads remain; this is not a paint-stripping or structural repair operation.
verification: Footrest assemblies and lower roller removed; remaining frame attachments recorded.

steps.title: Inspect the exposed main frame
steps.instruction: Clean and inspect the exposed main frame with both steering head races removed; retain bonded pads and identification markings. Record cracks, bends, thread/seat damage, corrosion or fretting. Structural repair, race-seat machining and alignment correction are outside this route. Confirm the frame is serviceable before installing races or continuing the following bench renewal stages.
verification: Frame condition and component repair status recorded; no structural fault silently accepted.

steps.title: Expose both sides of the hub
steps.instruction: Record the installed disc and sprocket faces/orientations before removal. Support the wheel without loading the disc. Remove the six sprocket self-locking nuts and retain the bolt/washer arrangement by location; remove the sprocket. Remove the six brake-disc bolts and lift off the disc. Keep friction surfaces clear of grease and locking agent.
verification: Sprocket/disc orientation and hardware recorded; hub accessible; disc protected.

steps.title: Remove seals and bearing retention
steps.instruction: Clean the hub exterior. Lever out both old oil seals with a flat-head screwdriver, using a cloth between tool and wheel to protect the hub. Remove the right-side bearing circlip with suitable circlip pliers before attempting to extract that bearing. Retain old seals and clip only for matching replacements.
verification: Both seals and right-side circlip removed; bearing retention released.

steps.title: Extract all three old bearings
steps.instruction: Use an appropriate bearing puller as Yamaha specifies. Remove the single right-side bearing and retain the internal spacer; extract both left-side bearings. Keep their side/order identified against PDF135/137. Support the hub for the puller reaction; do not force a bearing against retained hardware or damage its housing.
verification: Three old bearings removed: right one, left two; internal spacer retained.

steps.title: Inspect the hub and spacer
steps.instruction: Clean and inspect bearing seats, circlip groove, internal spacer and external collars for damage or wear. Record whether the original hub and spacer remain serviceable. Check axle bending on a flat surface; do not straighten it. Check tire/wheel condition now; measure runout after the wheel is refitted on its axle as instructed in the final check. A damaged seat, spacer, axle, disc or worn sprocket requires its own repair/replacement decision; this guide does not authorize machining or truing.
verification: Hub/spacer/collars and axle condition recorded; no unresolved damage accepted; runout deferred until axle refit.

steps.title: Fit the right bearing first
steps.instruction: Identify the brake-disc/right side and the single matching new bearing. Install it first into its original seat, pressing the outer race square and parallel with a correctly sized driver/socket. Follow the PDF137 arrangement and general marked-face-outward orientation. Do not drive through the inner race or use compressed air to spin the bearing.
verification: Right-side new bearing square in its original seat; correct side and marked-face orientation checked.

steps.title: Fit new right-side retention
steps.instruction: Install the matching new circlip into the right-side hub groove. Follow the general PDF25 edge/force orientation and exact PDF135/137 retaining position; do not overexpand it. Verify the full circumference is seated in the groove before covering it with the seal. If bearing position prevents seating, correct the assembly rather than forcing the clip.
verification: New circlip fully seated; bearing retained; edge orientation checked.

steps.title: Restore the spacer and both left bearings
steps.instruction: Insert the original serviceable internal spacer in the PDF137 position between the right bearing and left bearing pair. Fit both matching new left-side bearings in the order/positions shown in PDF135/137. Press each outer race square and parallel with a matching driver. Keep the spacer correctly located; do not omit it or force a cocked bearing. Verify the stack and smooth bearing rotation before installing seals.
verification: Internal spacer present; two left bearings installed; all three bearings turn smoothly and stack matches drawing.

steps.title: Install both new wheel seals
steps.instruction: Apply lithium-soap-based grease to both new seal lips. Face their manufacturer marks/numbers outward and the main lips toward the hub interior. Drive each seal evenly using a socket/driver matching its outside diameter. Set both at the approximate1.0 mm recess shown by dimension a in the two PDF135 cross-sections; do not copy the front-wheel flush setting. Measure and record each recess against the illustrated hub-face reference.
verification: Both new seals oriented and undamaged; left/right approximate1.0 mm recess recorded.

steps.title: Refit the original serviceable sprocket
steps.instruction: Clean the hub/sprocket mating faces and restore the recorded original orientation and bolt/washer arrangement. This workflow uses matching new self-locking nuts. Tighten all six nuts progressively in a crisscross pattern to42 N·m. Inspect that the sprocket sits fully against the hub. Worn or bent teeth require matched drive/rear sprocket replacement outside this retained-sprocket operation.
verification: Six sprocket nuts42 N·m in staged crisscross pattern; mating faces seated.

steps.title: Refit the original serviceable disc
steps.instruction: Restore the recorded disc orientation against clean mating faces. Apply the specified LOCTITE locking agent at the disc-bolt threads and tighten all six bolts progressively in a crisscross pattern to12 N·m. The OEM source does not identify a grade or cure time here; record the actual product and follow its instructions. Keep grease/locking agent away from friction faces and inspect seating.
verification: Six disc bolts12 N·m in stages/crisscross; actual locking agent recorded; disc seated and friction faces clean.

steps.title: Inspect the removed wheel
steps.instruction: Roll the axle on a flat surface and replace it if bent; never straighten it. Inspect wheel, tire, disc and collars. Record bearing roughness or looseness and seal damage. Continue this bearing-renewal route only with a serviceable hub and no unresolved tire, rim, spoke or disc defect.
verification: Bearing/seal findings recorded; remaining wheel assembly is serviceable.

steps.title: Remove both oil seals
steps.instruction: Clean the outside of the hub. Use a flat-head screwdriver to lift out the oil seals, with a cloth between the screwdriver and hub to protect the wheel surface. Discard both removed seals.
verification: Both seals removed without damaging the hub.

steps.title: Pull both hub bearings
steps.instruction: Use a suitable bearing puller to remove both bearings. Retain the centre spacer and keep the left and right locations identified. Discard the removed bearings; do not load or bend the retained brake disc.
verification: Both bearings removed; centre spacer retained.

steps.title: Check the hub and spacer
steps.instruction: Confirm the bearing bores and spacer have not been damaged and are clean enough for the new bearings to seat correctly. A damaged or loose bearing fit needs separate wheel repair; do not conceal it with an improvised shim or adhesive.
verification: Record accepted hub/spacer condition or stop for wheel repair.

steps.title: Install the left bearing first
steps.instruction: Fit the new LEFT bearing first with its manufacturer marks or size symbols facing outward. Press it squarely by its outer race using a matching driver or socket, following the bearing position in the assembly diagram.
verification: Left bearing seated squarely; pressing load applied only to its outer race.

steps.title: Restore the spacer and right bearing
steps.instruction: Insert the centre spacer, then install the new RIGHT bearing with its manufacturer marks or size symbols facing outward. Press squarely on its outer race with the matching driver. Confirm the spacer remains correctly positioned between the bearings and the bearing seats as illustrated.
verification: Spacer present; right bearing squarely seated.

steps.title: Install both new oil seals
steps.instruction: Apply lithium-soap-based grease to the seal lips. Install each new seal with its manufacturer marks or numbers facing OUTWARD. Use a driver/socket matching the seal diameter. Set each seal flush at the illustrated 0 mm depth shown in the page 4-8 cross-section.
verification: Both new seals face outward and have the illustrated flush 0 mm seating.

steps.title: Check the renewed hub
steps.instruction: Turn the bearings and verify smooth movement without looseness. Confirm both seals and the centre spacer are correctly located before the side collars and axle are fitted. Resolve binding or a loose fit before returning the wheel to the bike.
verification: Record smooth bearings, no looseness and all internal parts present.

steps.title: Identify every bearing and seal stack
steps.instruction: Photograph both swingarm ends and each linkage joint against Yamaha PDF187/193. Remove collars, seals, thrust bearings, bushes and washers in illustrated order, retaining identified serviceable washers separately. The swingarm has four pivot bearings; the relay arm has four and connecting arm two. Do not mix washer groups or press against a retained seal, collar or bush.
verification: All stacks mapped to source diagram
Four swingarm and six linkage bearings identified

source_links.title: Yamaha exact bearing stack and depths

steps.title: Remove bearings with supported fitting tools
steps.instruction: Use Motion Pro08-0294 figures1-2/5 for accessible bearings: select a fitting driver, center the receiver and draw each bearing into the cup. Where opposite-side access is unavailable, figures7-8 show the fully engaged blind remover with greased puller threads/washer. First remove obstructions and check for hidden retainers. Stop if the receiver cannot support the housing squarely. Clean and inspect every empty bore.
verification: Tool fit/support and unobstructed removal path checked
Bores undamaged; no retained debris

source_links.title: Yamaha exact bearing stack and depths
Motion Pro tool technique; Yamaha depths control

steps.title: Install the four pivot bearings to Yamaha depths
steps.instruction: Pack bearings and lubricate the pivot bearing stack with molybdenum-disulfide grease. Motion Pro figures3-4 show a matching mandrel supporting needles during installation. Yamaha PDF194 requires outer bearings first, then inner bearings to the illustrated depths measured from inside. Use PDF193/195 cross-sections: inner bearing position dimension b is6.5mm. Record both sides. Yamaha depths control; do not substitute the CRF example tool-bottoming endpoint.
verification: Four bearings installed outer then inner
Both6.5mm reference dimensions measured at exact OEM section
No needle loss, cocking or damage

source_links.title: Yamaha exact bearing stack and depths
Motion Pro tool technique; Yamaha depths control

steps.title: Complete pivot bushes, thrust bearings and seals
steps.instruction: Restore the two correct new matched bushes, two thrust bearings, four new oil seals and inspected collars in Yamaha PDF193/195 order. Lubricate with molybdenum-disulfide grease. Measure the four illustrated seal recesses a:0–0.5mm from their respective bore faces. Use the cross-section for lip orientation and the general seal markings guidance; do not use the6.5mm bearing depth for a seal. Record each seal depth and stack.
verification: Two bushes/two thrust bearings/four seals accounted for
Four a depths0–0.5mm recorded
Seals undamaged and correctly oriented

source_links.title: Yamaha exact bearing stack and depths

steps.title: Renew both relay-arm bearing pairs
steps.instruction: Install the four relay bearings using fitting mandrels and supported housing. Yamaha PDF187/189 specifies0mm bearing depth at the illustrated end faces. Lubricate bearings, washers, seals and collars with molybdenum-disulfide grease. Restore inner washers, four new seals, matched collars and outer washers in the exact exploded/cross-section order. Record bearing flushness and both four-washer groups; the bearing0mm dimension is not a generic seal-depth instruction.
verification: Four relay bearings at source0mm faces
Four inner and four outer washers correctly grouped
Four new seals and two matched collars installed

source_links.title: Yamaha exact bearing stack and depths

steps.title: Renew connecting-arm bearings
steps.instruction: Install the two connecting-arm bearings at the0mm bearing locations illustrated on Yamaha PDF187/189. Use molybdenum-disulfide grease at the exploded-diagram marked bearing/seal/collar surfaces. Restore two new seals and the matched collar with source orientation. Record both bearing positions and smooth collar movement; do not infer a seal depth from the bearing dimension.
verification: Two connecting bearings flush at specified faces
Two new seals and matched collar installed
No binding or displaced seal

source_links.title: Yamaha exact bearing stack and depths

steps.title: Record and expose the two mount stacks
steps.instruction: Photograph Yamaha PDF186 upper and lower stack orientations. Remove each pair of collars and dust seals; remove the upper O-rings. Identify the upper stopper ring and remove it before pressing the upper bushing. Lower eye has its separate bushing and bearing. Keep each eye supported locally and all spring/pressure components untouched.
verification: Upper/lower stacks identified separately
Upper stopper removed before bushing extraction
Spring, rod and pressure body not loaded

steps.title: Remove worn eye bearing components
steps.instruction: Use fitting mandrels and a centered receiver as in Motion Pro08-0294 figures1-2/5 to remove the upper bushing and lower bearing/bushing without stressing the shock rod or body. Verify the extraction path is unobstructed. Clean the empty seats and inspect for damage. A damaged mounting eye needs assembly repair/replacement beyond this operation; do not enlarge or stake the seat.
verification: Fitting local support recorded
No bore damage, retained fragments or obstructions

source_links.title: Motion Pro supported bearing tool technique only

steps.title: Install and retain upper bushing
steps.instruction: Press the upper bushing squarely by its outer race until its stopper-ring groove is exposed, as Yamaha PDF190 specifies. Install a new correct stopper ring fully in the groove. Push the bushing back until it contacts the ring. Lubricate the two new O-rings with lithium-soap grease, and restore the upper seals and collars in PDF186 order and orientation.
verification: Stopper seated fully
Bushing returned into contact with stopper
Two new O-rings and two new seals correctly installed

steps.title: Renew lower bearing and seal stack
steps.instruction: Install the new lower bearing/bushing and correct collars to the exact PDF186/190 section. Apply molybdenum-disulfide grease to the lower bearing and dust seals, but keep the bearing outer race dry: Yamaha warns greasing this press fit wears the shock seating surface. Fit two new dust seals with lips inward. Measure each source-labelled a dimension at the collar/seal cross-section: at least0.3mm. This is not an invented bearing insertion depth. Record both sides and smooth collar movement.
verification: Outer race and press-fit seat kept dry
Both seal lips inward
Both a measurements at least0.3mm at source locations
Correct bearing/bushing/collars complete

steps.title: Install both new head races
steps.instruction: Use Motion Pro08-0669 page1 photographs for assembly. Clean the seats; test each new race on its driver. Fit tapered plate, washer and greased threaded rod with all nut threads engaged. Position the correctly oriented race/driver, pass the rod through, engage the locking plate and hand-snug. Draw in with24mm wrench, holding rod with14mm if needed. Watch alignment throughout; stop at the fully seated shoulder when resistance increases. Release and remove the tool; repeat for the other race. Unexpected resistance before seating requires inspection, not extra force.
verification: Both race orientations match Yamaha diagram
Both races aligned and fully seated; tool fit and observed seat condition recorded

steps.title: Install the lower seal and bearing
steps.instruction: Follow Motion Pro08-0544 page1 installation photographs. Clean stem and bracket seat. Restore the correct new dust seal before the bearing. Apply Yamaha lithium-soap grease to seal lip and bearing inner circumference. Select driver contacting only the inner race, clear of cage; use the HF adapter if required. Support the bracket underside on a protective block. Remove the tool puller bolt and use a soft mallet to seat the new bearing. Inspect full seating and intact seal/cage; grease the bearing.
verification: Correct seal stack installed before bearing
Driver loaded inner race only
Full bearing seating and undamaged seal/cage recorded

steps.title: Restore footrests, roller and retained mounting pieces
steps.instruction: Return all labeled rubber pieces and clip-in holders to their original positions. Refit the intact footrest brackets with source-specified LOCTITE on the four bolts and tighten55 N·m. Refit the intact lower chain-tensioner roller and collar stack and tighten its bolt16 N·m; check the roller turns correctly.
verification: Footrest bolts55 N·m; lower roller16 N·m and free; original mount pieces restored.

steps.title: Reinstall the rear frame and upper roller
steps.instruction: Align the supported rear frame without trapping wires. Return its four bolts to their mapped positions and tighten38 N·m. Install the upper chain tensioner and washer on its correct bolt, then install a new retaining pin through the outside pin hole as illustrated; the inside hole is the documented alternative if necessary. Bend the pin so its tip stays within the roller's outer diameter.
verification: Four rear-frame bolts38 N·m; roller/washer/new pin correctly retained.

steps.title: Place the controls, loom and brackets back on the frame
steps.instruction: Place the separately supported throttle-body/cable group and bar/control/hydraulic assemblies near their original locations, keeping them independently supported until mounted. Route the main loom along the original frame/tank-rail path and engage its locating projections. Refit the original air-filter-case brackets, rectifier/regulator and ignition-coil bracket at7 N·m for each respective mounting bolt. Do not disturb sensor or throttle adjustment screws. Use the exact diagram rather than crossing the loom over the engine opening.
verification: Bracket mount groups7 N·m; loom located; unsupported units still protected.

steps.title: Restore rear harness routing and holders
steps.instruction: Restore the harness/starter-lead ties at the white and green tape locations. At the green-tape clip, starter lead lies below the harness; lock faces down and trimmed end outward. Route negative lead along the inside of the starter lead, and positive lead outside the rear-fender projection. Reseat ECU/CCU/relay connectors and covers: ECU holder enters its battery-box bracket with ECU connector toward the left. Fit the battery and band but leave terminal leads isolated until final startup preparation. At the white-tape rear-frame tie, point the lock downward and trimmed end outward as well.
verification: Rear tie locations/orientations and ECU/CCU/relay holders/covers restored; battery remains isolated.

steps.title: Mount the radiators and route their hoses
steps.instruction: Inspect hoses and mounting dampers for damage. Restore the original damper/collar/washer stacks and tighten the four radiator mounting bolts10 N·m. Return hoses1–4 to their labeled radiator ends, preserving the original clamp positions; disturbed hose-clamp screws tighten1.5 N·m. Leave engine-end joints ready for engine installation. Route radiator breather behind the upper boss, ahead of the lower boss and ahead of the radiator hose, then through the down tube as shown.
verification: Radiator mounts10 N·m; radiator-side clamps1.5 N·m; breather and hoses correctly routed.

steps.title: Hang the intact shock on its upper mount
steps.instruction: Verify the completed new upper bushing/stopper/seals and correctly seated collars and lubricate the upper mounting bolt with molybdenum-disulfide grease. Install the bolt from the right and tighten its nut56 N·m. Keep the sealed shock supported until its lower connection is restored; no preload or internal changes are implied.
verification: Upper bolt from right; nut56 N·m; new bushing/stopper/O-rings/seals and correct collars verified.

steps.title: Lubricate the bearing stack
steps.instruction: Apply lithium-soap-based grease to the bearings, dust-seal/race-cover lips, steering-stem threads and the stem portion shown in the OEM illustration. Return the lower bracket with its newly fitted lower bearing, install the NEW matching upper bearing and race cover in the illustrated order. Fit the ring nut with its stepped side downward.
verification: Lubricated bearing/cover stack correct; ring-nut step faces down.

steps.title: Set the steering preload
steps.instruction: Hold the torque wrench at a right angle to the steering-nut wrench. Tighten the ring nut initially to 38 N·m and turn the steering left/right several times. If it binds, inspect the bearings. Loosen the ring nut one full turn, then retighten to 7 N·m. Check full lock-to-lock movement without play or binding.
verification: Initial 38 N·m, loosen one turn, final 7 N·m; smooth steering without looseness.

steps.title: Restore the upper bracket and stem nut
steps.instruction: Install the washer and upper bracket. Slide the fork legs into place and temporarily secure the lower clamps, leaving the upper pinch bolts loose. Grease the steering-stem nut contact surface with lithium-soap grease and tighten the stem nut to 145 N·m. Check steering again; if movement is not smooth, follow the manual ring-nut adjustment rather than proceeding.
verification: Washer fitted; stem nut 145 N·m; steering smooth.

steps.title: Refit and secure the top assemblies
steps.instruction: With the legs temporarily held by the lower clamps and the upper pinch bolts still loose, tighten each damper assembly at the top to 30 N·m using the cap ring wrench. Keep each leg supported.
verification: Legs supported; top damper assemblies 30 N·m; upper clamps still loose.

steps.title: Set height and tighten the clamps
steps.instruction: With each leg supported, set its outer-tube top projection to 2 mm using the exact source-diagram reference. Match both sides. Tighten upper and lower clamp pinch bolts to 21 N·m; do not overtorque the lower clamps.
verification: Both projections 2 mm; all upper/lower pinch bolts 21 N·m.

steps.title: Restore the handlebar and fender
steps.instruction: Refit the front fender with its four bolts at 10 N·m. Refit the handlebar at its recorded marks with upper-holder punch marks forward and equal side-to-side marks. Tighten the front upper-holder bolts first, then the rear bolts, to 28 N·m. Keep the lower holders unchanged. Check bar alignment and cable/hose clearance now; verify fuel-tank clearance after tank reinstallation.
verification: Fender 10 N·m; holders 28 N·m front first; original bar position and free movement.

steps.title: Lubricate the sliding and cable-end surfaces
steps.instruction: Apply lithium-soap-based grease to the throttle-grip sliding surface. Lightly grease the cable ends and inside of the grip as shown. Keep grease away from the exterior gripping surface and the brake.
verification: Sliding and cable-end contact surfaces lubricated.

steps.title: Reconnect pull and return cables
steps.instruction: Restore each identified cable end to its original seat and groove in the throttle tube. Place the rubber cover and slide the intact grip/tube onto the handlebar. Confirm both cable ends and their outer housings are seated correctly before closing the housing.
verification: Both cable ends seated in the correct positions without crossing.

steps.title: Secure the housing
steps.instruction: Fit the housing and tighten its screws to 3.8 Nm. Check grip movement immediately. If the housing causes binding, reposition and retighten it, then check again. Restore the housing cover and rubber cover.
verification: Housing torqued; grip moves smoothly and returns.

steps.title: Restore protectors and brake mounts
steps.instruction: Refit the protectors at 7 N·m per bolt. Refit the complete caliper to the fork and tighten its two mount bolts to 28 N·m. Align the upper end of the hose holder with the hose paint mark and tighten its bolts to 9 N·m, preserving the original routing.
verification: Protectors 7 / caliper 28 / hose-holder 9 N·m; hose aligned and unstressed.

steps.title: Install the wheel and axle
steps.instruction: Apply lithium-soap grease to the axle and wheel oil-seal lips. Put the side-specific collars back, lift the wheel into place with the disc correctly between the pads, and insert the axle. Thread the axle nut on by hand; leave its final tightening and the axle pinch bolts for the seating step.
verification: Collars correct; disc between pads; axle inserted; nut retained; final torques pending.

steps.title: Restore front control routing
steps.instruction: Route the throttle cables to the right of the number-plate bracket and the starter-switch lead to its left. Both switch leads pass between the plate routing section and upper bracket. Match the plate markings and drawing: clutch hose on the right, ahead of throttle cables and behind the front brake hose. Restore bar ties with locks downward and ends forward, clear of masters and fork tubes. The front brake hose then returns to the plate guides in the next step.
verification: Cable/lead sides and hose crossing order match the source; ties cannot contact controls or forks.

steps.title: Verify free play and return before starting
steps.instruction: With the engine stopped, check free play and smooth full return through the steering travel. The retained setup must still have 3–6 mm free play and no binding. If not, correct seating/routing before starting; do not use a running engine to diagnose a bound throttle.
verification: Record 3–6 mm free play and full return at centre and both steering limits.

steps.title: Restore guides and settings
steps.instruction: Engage the number-plate projection in the front fender, route the hose through both plate guides and tighten the number-plate bolt to 7 N·m. Restore the recorded rebound and compression settings using the gently seated full-hard reference; verify left/right settings match the intended setup.
verification: Plate 7 N·m; both guides used; original damping settings logged and restored.

steps.title: Verify the engine and rear bearing stacks
steps.instruction: Confirm any independently performed internal engine work has documented pre-start clearance, timing and free-rotation checks; this route leaves engine internals assembled. Verify all renewed swingarm bearing/bush/thrust/seal depths and stack records. Grease their specified contact surfaces with molybdenum-disulfide grease and position the supported swingarm with its correct renewed side stacks. The single shared pivot next locates both arm and engine; do not install a second pivot or repeat engine removal.
verification: Engine bench record verified; arm stacks lubricated and supported for shared pivot.

steps.title: Place the engine back in the chassis
steps.instruction: Bring the supported engine in from the right and align its mounting points without trapping wires/hoses. Apply molybdenum-disulfide grease to the pivot; install it from the right and restore the swingarm support stack. Apply lithium-soap grease to the pivot-nut threads and contact face.
verification: Engine aligned from right; pivot from right; supports and grease correct.

steps.title: Install and secure the engine brackets
steps.instruction: Restore the original lower and upper brackets and mapped hardware. Follow the labeled engine-install drawing: pivot nut 75 N·m; lower engine-mount bolt 53 N·m; front bracket bolts 34 N·m; front engine-mount bolt 55 N·m; upper bracket bolts 34 N·m; upper engine-mount bolts 45 N·m. Keep the supported assembly aligned while tightening.
verification: All six distinct mounting torque groups recorded against the diagram.

steps.title: Refit the linkage in its original orientation
steps.instruction: Lubricate the circumferences and threads of the three linkage bolts and lower shock bolt with molybdenum-disulfide grease. Fit the connecting-arm frame bolt from the right; connecting-arm relay bolt, relay-arm swingarm bolt and lower shock bolt from the left. Restore the correct renewed matched collars and inspected washers in their identified joints. Raise the arm to align the lower shock without forcing the bolts.
verification: Original linkage orientation and washer stacks restored; bolt directions matched.

steps.title: Secure the linkage and lower shock
steps.instruction: Tighten the connecting-arm frame nut and connecting-arm relay nut to 80 N·m each. Tighten the relay-arm swingarm nut to 70 N·m and the lower shock nut to 53 N·m. The upper shock mount was separately restored to56 N·m in this frame sequence; verify that recorded check.
verification: Frame 80, relay 80, swingarm 70, lower shock 53 N·m recorded.

steps.title: Mount the closed rear brake assembly
steps.instruction: Refit the rear master cylinder to its frame mount with both mounting bolts10 N·m, keeping its original pushrod/clevis adjustment unchanged. Restore the hose along the swingarm: paint mark up, no interference with the spring or suspension. Seat each retaining clamp fully, latch by at least three notches and face the clamp opening inward. Keep caliper/bracket supported for wheel insertion. Pedal pivot/spring are restored by the engine closure step next.
verification: Master mount bolts10 N·m; closed hose correctly routed; pedal/clevis unchanged.

steps.title: Restore the clutch release unit
steps.instruction: Replace the mounting O-ring and lubricate it and the pushrod contact end with silicone grease. Restore the retained washer and seat the release cylinder. Apply specified LOCTITE treatment to the two mount bolts and torque to 10 N·m. Keep hose unions and bleed screw untouched.
verification: New O-ring/washer correct; mount bolts 10 N·m; hydraulic line closed.

steps.title: Restore pedal, guard and breather
steps.instruction: Restore the brake-pedal pivot and spring, lubricating the illustrated pivot/seal contact locations with lithium-soap grease; tighten its bolt 26 N·m. Refit the engine guard at 7 N·m. Route the head breather between the two front bracket bolts and rear bracket bolt, with its paint marks within the holder/clamp areas.
verification: Pedal 26/guard 7 N·m; spring attached; breather routing and marks correct.

steps.title: Restore the drive sprocket and chain
steps.instruction: Refit the original sprocket with a new lock washer. Apply source-specified LOCTITE to the sprocket nut, tighten it 90 N·m and bend the washer tabs against its flats. Align shift-shaft/pedal punch marks and tighten the pedal bolt 12 N·m. Refit the cover at 7 N·m. Fit the stock chain using its matched link/plate and a new clip with closed end leading chain travel.
verification: Sprocket 90 and lock tabs; shift 12; cover 7; new correctly oriented chain clip.

steps.title: Refit the wheel and chain
steps.instruction: Grease the oil-seal lips with lithium-soap-based grease and refit the collars. Place the disc between the brake pads and locate the caliper bracket correctly in its swingarm guide. Push the wheel forward and put the chain onto the sprocket. Fit the left puller and insert the greased axle from the left.
verification: Collars retained; bracket engaged; disc between pads; chain on sprocket; axle from left.

steps.title: Fit the right puller and nut
steps.instruction: Fit the right chain puller, washer and axle nut. Leave the nut temporarily snug until chain adjustment is complete.
verification: Right puller and washer present; axle nut temporary only.

steps.title: Restore the engine ground and starter lead
steps.instruction: Refit the ground terminal at the cylinder-head location shown and tighten its bolt 7 N·m; point the lead upward and route it outside the high-tension cord. Refit the starter lead at 6 N·m while holding the motor-side nut with a spanner. Restore its clamp without slack, as shown.
verification: Head ground 7 N·m and upward; starter 6 N·m with terminal counterheld.

steps.title: Reconnect and route the engine harness
steps.instruction: Reconnect stator, crankshaft-position, gear-position and coolant-temperature connectors and their covers. Route stator/gear leads outside the head breather; stator lead passes behind the radiator without pinch. Keep clutch hose outside those leads and secure the original lower/upper tie positions shown. Install the plug cap fully against the cover; route ground/temperature/high-tension leads outside the breather. Replace released ties in the diagram directions. At the lower engine tie between the indicated left-cover bolts, point the lock outward. At the tie above the upper radiator boss, point the lock forward. Keep rectifier/regulator leads inside the tension arm and throttle cables behind the switch leads; align clutch-hose paint marks to the forward-facing clamp.
verification: Every labeled connector latched/covered; source routing and tie locations verified.

steps.title: Reseat the throttle body
steps.instruction: Remove intake protection and seat the intact throttle body fully in its original engine-side joint. Restore the clamp orientation and tighten the throttle-body joint clamp to 3.0 N·m. Keep both cables routed without tension and check full smooth throttle return. Sensors and calibration screws remain untouched.
verification: Joint fully seated 3.0 N·m; throttle returns smoothly; cables not trapped.

steps.title: Reconnect the engine coolant hoses
steps.instruction: Remove temporary port covers. Restore radiator hoses 1,3 and 4 to their marked engine connections and original clamp positions; tighten each disturbed radiator-hose clamp screw to 1.5 N·m. Check there are no kinks or trapped hoses. Radiator pipe seals and temperature sensor were not removed.
verification: Hoses 1/3/4 correct; disturbed clamps 1.5 N·m.

steps.title: Seat the new header gasket
steps.instruction: Install the new gasket at the head and refit header pipe 1. Tighten all header nuts first to 7 N·m, then retighten them to 10 N·m. Do not apply the protector-screw locking-agent note to these nuts.
verification: New head gasket; all header nuts 7 then 10 N·m.

steps.title: Locate pipe 2 and its clamp
steps.instruction: Install the new pipe-joint gaskets in their PDF206 positions. Refit the pipe-2 clamp, pipe 2 and bracket bolt. At each joint, engage the clamp projection in the pipe/silencer slot and keep the clamp off the raised projection illustrated in PDF212. Leave final bracket and clamp tightening until the silencer is seated.
verification: Fresh joint seals seated; clamp locating features correct.

steps.title: Refit the complete silencer
steps.instruction: Refit the silencer clamp and complete silencer on the seated joint. Install the retained mounting hardware and tighten both silencer mounting bolts to 30 N·m.
verification: Both silencer mounts 30 N·m; joints fully engaged.

steps.title: Tighten the bracket and both clamps
steps.instruction: Confirm front and rear joints remain fully inserted while tightening the exhaust-pipe bracket bolt to 20 N·m, pipe-2 clamp bolt to 16 N·m and silencer clamp bolt to 16 N·m.
verification: Bracket 20 N·m; each joint clamp 16 N·m; projections correctly located.

steps.title: Seat the case and secure its mounts
steps.instruction: Remove the temporary inlet protection and seat the complete case fully on the throttle-body intake connection in its original orientation. Restore the original mounting collars, dampers and washers. Tighten the three case mounting bolts to 7 N·m and the air-filter-case joint clamp screw to 3 N·m. Confirm the joint lip is evenly seated and not folded. Reconnect the temperature-sensor coupler until its latch engages.
verification: Three mounts 7 N·m; joint clamp 3 N·m; joint fully seated; sensor connector latched.

steps.title: Verify the restored intake
steps.instruction: Check case support, full joint seating, wiring clearance and that all temporary intake protection has been removed. The filter and bracket stayed assembled; if either has moved or a seal cannot be accounted for, resolve it before closing the bike.
verification: Intake complete and clean; retained assembly bracket/element secure.

steps.title: Reconnect the fuel system
steps.instruction: Refit the tank on its retained dampers/collars. Tighten its two front mounting bolts to 8 N·m and the tank retaining screw to 4 N·m. Remove the temporary joint covers, push the fuel hose fully onto the pipe until it clicks, and slide the connector cover back into its locked position. Keep the hose holder correctly oriented, with no kink or pinch. Reconnect the pump plug.
verification: Tank front bolts 8 N·m/retaining screw 4 N·m; hose latched/covered/routed; pump plug connected.

steps.title: Refill with the specified mixture
steps.instruction: Use the specified aluminum-compatible ethylene-glycol antifreeze and distilled water at a final 1:1 coolant-to-water ratio. Do not mix antifreeze types. Fill to the maximum level illustrated in PDF106. The complete system nominal volume is 1.03 L including all routes; correct level and concentration govern, not forcing in that amount after an incomplete drain. Wash any spill on paint away immediately with water.
verification: Mixture/product and amount recorded; level at illustrated maximum.

steps.title: Secure the radiator cap
steps.instruction: Install and secure the radiator cap. Account for the drain hardware, collection container and tools before running the engine.
verification: Cap secured; drain sealed; tools clear.

steps.title: Pressure-check the reinstalled cooling system
steps.instruction: With coolant at the upper level, install the specified radiator tester/adapter and apply137.3 kPa; do not exceed that pressure. It must hold5–10 seconds. Check radiator joints and hoses for leaks or bulging, correct any fault, release pressure and cover the connection with a cloth before removing the tester. Secure the radiator cap. Do not perform this check on a hot pressurized system.
verification: Cooling system holds137.3 kPa for5–10 seconds; no leaks/bulges; cap restored.

steps.title: Refill the oil for the actual engine condition
steps.instruction: Record the applicable oil quantity:0.94 L for oil change with unchanged filter,0.96 L with filter removal, or 1.20 L for a disassembled engine. Use the OEM-listed Yamalube/API SG-or-higher JASO MA oil; choose 10W-40,10W-50,15W-40,20W-40 or 20W-50 against the linked temperature chart; do not add friction modifiers or energy-conserving oil. Fit the filler cap with a new O-ring. Final level/flow checks remain required.
verification: Actual engine condition, oil grade and measured fill recorded; new filler O-ring.

steps.title: Reconnect the battery and inspect routing
steps.instruction: Recheck all engine interfaces, then reconnect positive battery lead before negative. Restore positive-terminal cover and the exact illustrated lead routing, with positive lead below negative. Keep all loose conductors away from the frame and secure the original connections.
verification: Positive then negative restored; terminal cover/routing correct.

steps.title: Refit the panels and seat
steps.instruction: Locate the radiator-guard projections in the shroud holes, then install the shrouds at 7 N·m. Refit the air-filter-case cover by engaging its projection and both ribs. Slide side-cover tabs into their slots; the right-cover rib sits under the rear-fender rib. Tighten ordinary left/right side-cover bolts to 7 N·m and the two seat bolts to 13 N·m. Refit the sub-seat with its tether untwisted, then press, rotate and secure its quick fastener.
verification: Tabs/ribs seated; shrouds/side-cover bolts 7 N·m; seat bolts 13 N·m; quick fastener locked.

steps.title: Measure and adjust chain slack
steps.instruction: Loosen the rear axle nut and both adjuster locknuts first. With the rear wheel raised and gearbox in neutral, pull the chain upward above the chain-guide mounting bolt with about 50 N. Measure between the drive-chain guide and the bottom of the chain at the exact diagram location. Adjust both sides equally to 50–60 mm. Push the wheel forward so each puller/end plate is seated against the swingarm end.
verification: Measured slack 50–60 mm using OEM50 N reference; pullers equally adjusted and seated.

steps.title: Secure the rear axle and adjusters
steps.instruction: Tighten the rear axle nut to 135 N·m and both chain-adjuster locknuts to 21 N·m. Recheck the chain slack after tightening.
verification: Axle 135 N·m; locknuts 21 N·m; final slack recorded.

steps.title: Check chain alignment and brake function
steps.instruction: Turn the wheel and check the chain follows the sprockets, the brake disc sits correctly and the rear brake has normal firm operation. Record wheel installation and any unresolved fault before use. With the wheel refitted on its axle and supported off the ground, secure a dial gauge and rotate the wheel to measure radial and lateral runout at the rim locations illustrated in PDF131. Record both readings; each rear-wheel limit is2.0 mm. Out-of-limit runout needs separate repair or replacement before use. Confirm there is no bearing roughness or free play after final axle torque; save bearing/seal replacements, both seal recesses and the retention/spacer checks. Any binding after tightening remains an unresolved assembly fault.
verification: Final axle-supported radial/lateral runout readings, bearing rotation/play, chain alignment/slack and brake function recorded; all renewal and retention checks saved.

steps.title: Seat the forks before final axle tightening
steps.instruction: With the bike securely supported on its wheels, push down on the handlebars several times and confirm smooth fork rebound before final axle-nut tightening, as Yamaha specifies. Tighten the axle nut to 115 N·m, then all four axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m. This is a stationary seating operation, not permission to ride with loose axle hardware.
verification: Smooth rebound before nut torque; axle nut 115 N·m; four axle pinch bolts 21 N·m.

steps.title: Verify steering and front-end closure
steps.instruction: Check the rebuilt steering and front end now: no play or binding, smooth fork action, wheel correctly secured and firm front brake. Inspect hose/cable clearance while the remaining assemblies are still supported. Repeat whole-bike checks after the remaining fluid and startup checks are complete.
verification: No play/binding; fork and brake normal; cable/hose clearance and final readings recorded.

steps.title: Restore fuel and verify readiness to start
steps.instruction: Open the sub-seat access and add clean recommended unleaded gasoline, minimum 91 (R+M)/2; E10 is permitted. Secure the fuel cap and sub-seat fastener with its tether untwisted. Check the pump connector and latched fuel hose/cover, and check for fuel leaks. Select neutral and work in a ventilated area before any starter operation.
verification: Correct fuel restored; cap/fastener secured; hose/connector checked; no fuel leak; neutral selected.

steps.title: Verify oil flow immediately at idle
steps.instruction: Start only after fuel, intake, cooling, electrical and mounting closure is complete. Keep the engine at idle; observe the oil-check window for oil flow and decreasing level. If the level does not decrease, stop the engine immediately and investigate the lubrication system instead of revving it.
verification: Oil flow/level decrease observed at idle; no leak or abnormal condition.

steps.title: Warm for the operating checks
steps.instruction: After initial idle oil-flow verification and with all fuel, cooling, intake and control closure complete, warm the engine for several minutes. Leave the radiator cap secured. Proceed to the following measured operating checks before stopping and cooling completely.
verification: Initial oil flow verified; engine warmed for the next measured operating checks; cap remains closed.

steps.title: Check the warm idle
steps.instruction: Use the correctly configured YDT 90890-03275 (US USB) or 90890-03273 to confirm coolant at 70–80 °C. Measure speed with tachometer 90890-06760 or YU-39951-B, connected as shown to the ignition-coil high-tension lead. With the starter knob fully returned and normal filter/compression/free play, verify 1900–2100 r/min. If necessary, adjust the idle screw; clockwise raises speed.
verification: Record temperature and accepted idle speed.

steps.title: Set the final grip free play
steps.instruction: Stop the engine. If final adjustment is needed after idle setting, loosen the grip adjuster locknut, turn the adjuster to obtain 3–6 mm free play, and tighten the locknut. Confirm smooth full return again.
verification: Record final 3–6 mm free play and secure locknut.

steps.title: Verify idle through steering travel
steps.instruction: Restart the warm engine without starter enrichment. Turn the handlebar fully left and right: idle must not change. If it changes, stop and correct cable routing/seating or adjustment before repeating this check. Hold the engine-stop switch until the engine fully stops when the check is finished.
verification: Record unchanged idle across steering travel; engine stopped.

steps.title: Allow complete cooling
steps.instruction: After the operating check has stopped the engine, let it cool completely before opening the radiator cap for the next cold-level check.
verification: Engine stopped and fully cooled before the cap is opened.

steps.title: Recheck the cold level
steps.instruction: Keep the bike upright on level ground. With the engine cooled, use the cloth and slow pressure-release method to remove the cap. Allow the coolant to settle, check against the illustrated maximum and add the correct mixture if low. Restore the cap securely. A leak or repeatedly dropping level requires repair rather than repeated top-offs.
verification: Final cold level and mixture recorded; cap secured; no unresolved loss.

steps.title: Verify the installed engine and record closure
steps.instruction: Follow the oil-level procedure with the bike upright: warm oil to normal operating temperature, run for 10 seconds, stop and allow a few minutes to settle; level must be between window minimum and maximum mark. Check leaks, normal clutch/brake operation, throttle free play 3–6 mm and full return; confirm the preceding recorded warm-idle steering test was completed without idle change. Record all mount torques, fluid quantities, chain slack and unresolved symptoms. Engine installation completion does not substitute for an internal rebuild record.
verification: Oil level/flow, coolant level, leak/control checks and hardware record complete.

steps.title: Verify the rebuilt chassis as a whole
steps.instruction: Check steering play and lock-to-lock clearance, smooth front/rear suspension, front/rear wheel retention and brake action, chain alignment/slack, footrest return and all disturbed frame/engine/linkage fasteners. Check the throttle returns and idle does not change when steering; inspect fuel/oil/coolant leaks and retained harness/tie clearances. Record every unresolved defect and completed separate engine/component job. This record documents reassembly of serviceable stock assemblies, not structural frame repair or automatic permission to ride. With the fuel tank installed, verify the handlebar does not contact it at either steering lock. Record both renewed wheel bearing stacks, front flush/rear approximate1mm seal depths, steering race seating, swingarm/linkage depths and sealed shock-eye retention. No listed renewal is completed by merely refitting its housing.
verification: Whole-bike mechanical/control/fluid checks recorded; unresolved faults remain open.

entry_state: Assembled exact stock bike; all renewal parts and fitting tools verified; original control setup recorded.
exit_state: Serviceable main frame reassembled after both steering race sets, both wheel bearing stacks, swingarm/linkage and shock-eye bearings renewed. One coordinated engine/pivot refit and one closure per wheel. Throttle ends restored; fluids, routing, torque, wheel runout and operating checks recorded.
